context: a letter from T. C. Eyton, which you are answering
exchanges:
I shall send per rail tomorrow of which I beg your acceptance a copy of my Osteologia avium now complete   I have otained several more rare skeletons since descrptions of which will form an appendix and will appear as soon as my eyes get well enough to work at them which I have no doubt they will as soon as cool weather comes as they are much better for the last cool day or two   What a capital address that was of Hookers at Norwich   I intended to have been there but eyes said no. I have amoung other skeletons obtained that of Opisthocomus cristatus a bird that has been placed in all sorts of places but is a true guan. Huxley borrowed of me and is I believe going to publish a paper on it in the zoological proceedings. I have got a lot of pigs heads from different parts   their variation is extraordinary. I sowed this year some convolvulus in front of the house   some of the blossoms on the same plant are pink some purple and some white.

yours truly | Tho C Eyton

Aug 23

I was very glad to see your hand-writing again, & I thank you sincerely for your intended present of your Osteology. How nobly & perseveringly you have stuck to your arduous task!

I had heard of your skeleton of Opisthocomus.— I am sorry to hear about your eyes. I shd. have very much liked to have been at Norwich; but my weak health rendered it impossible. Oh for those good old days when I hunted with your Harriers & fished at Eyton: those were happy times for me.

With many thanks & all good wishes   Believe me Dear Eyton | Yours very sincerely | Ch. Darwin
